approved_text: Find all pairs of natural numbers m < n such that some nondecreasing natural-number sequence stays complete after zeroing the terms at any m indices, but not after zeroing the terms at any n indices. Complete: every sufficiently large integer is a sum of distinct values of the sequence.
draft: Find all pairs of natural numbers m < n for which some nondecreasing sequence a_0 ≤ a_1 ≤ … of natural numbers has this property: replacing the terms at any m indices by 0 leaves a complete set of values, but doing so at any n indices does not. Complete means every sufficiently large integer is a sum of distinct elements.
source_docstrings:
For what values of $0 \leq m < n$ is there a complete sequence
$A = \{a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots\}$ of integers such that
 1. $A$ remains complete after removing any $m$ elements, but
 2. $A$ is not complete after removing any $n$ elements.

        (_ : ∀ t, t.card = n → ¬IsAddComplete (Set.range (Function.updateFinset a t 0))) } =
